a bit more
Teach a recipe without measurements.

Auntie said add flour until it feels right and I said that is not an amount. She had flour on her cheek and I didn't tell her because she'd already laughed at my scales. This was for forty people. Forty. I wanted some numbers. She tipped half the bag in and said now you know. Outside my cousins were arguing about who had borrowed the car and inside my mother was trying to make the oven work by hitting the knob. We had rented this hall because it had a kitchen. The kitchen had one tray and a knife that bent when you cut bread. Auntie pushed the bowl at me, said knead, went outside to join the car argument. I had never kneaded anything except that clay at school. It stuck right up my wrists. I tried scraping it off on the edge and dragged the bowl into my lap. Mum turned round at exactly that moment and said don't get stressed. I said I wasn't stressed. She looked at the dough on my trousers. I put it back in the bowl because nobody was going to see that bit, then immediately felt awful about it and took a handful out again, but which handful
He's here
Someone arrives unexpectedly for dinner.

We had already eaten when my brother came. He said he'd eaten too but looked at the pan every time someone moved. Mum offered to heat it up. No no. She put the pan on. Really I'm fine. She turned on the gas. We all know this conversation by heart. I got another plate and he sat down without taking his coat off. There was a cut under his chin and he kept touching it. Dad asked about the car. My brother said it was outside. Dad asked where outside. That's when I realised he hadn't come in his own car. Mum was stirring the pan much too fast and the sauce was sticking. I wanted everyone to just eat before we started again.
Cardamon
A recipe contains an unexplained ingredient.

I bit the pod and it filled my whole mouth with perfume. Spat it into my hand like a child. Gran said you're supposed to leave those. Nobody told me. The recipe just said add six. Add six what, little traps apparently.
Start again
Start dinner again.

Burned the onions. Started again. Burned those too because I was still chopping the other stuff. There must be a way people do all these things at once. I ate the tomato standing up and put the rest back in the fridge.
No good plates
An ordinary object breaks during a celebration.

The bowl's bottom fell off during Sam's speech. Rice on the cloth. My cousin started eating it and everyone laughed except the bride. Hired bowl, hired cloth, somebody would pay. I picked out china. Mum slapped my hand then used hers. Bride asked how much. Sam said don't worry. She asked again. Nobody had spoons now because Mum was collecting those for some reason. Sam tried to finish the speech but had forgotten where he'd got to.
Cake for breakfast
Eat something after the occasion has ended.

The icing had gone hard and the cake underneath was still wet. I don't understand how that happens. We cut around the part where someone had put out a cigarette. Dad said he hadn't done it, which nobody had asked. My sister was asleep on the sofa in her shoes. One of her earrings was stuck to the cushion. I tried pulling it free and she woke up swinging at me, not properly awake, just one arm. I ducked and the cake fell icing down on the carpet. Dad started laughing, a real ugly laugh with no breath in it. I sat on the floor and laughed too because I was too tired to do anything else. The dog came over and Dad caught him by the collar. Nobody was getting breakfast apparently. We still had all the chairs to take back before twelve.
Replacement hero
The chosen one cannot make it.

The chosen one had a dentist appointment so they sent me. This sounds stupid but he'd already cancelled twice and they'd charge him the full amount, which the prophecy budget apparantly didn't cover. I had his cloak and a letter saying I was acting on his behalf. The cave didn't accept letters. It spoke directly into my teeth, ALL WHO ENTER MUST BE NAMED, so I said Gus and it said WRONG. I tried his name. Wrong. Tried his full name including the middle bit he hated. Still wrong. By now the horse had started eating the letter and I was wondering if maybe named meant like given a special name by the gods. I said Sword of Morning. The cave made a noise that could have been a laugh. Behind me the horse said Gerald. The cave opened. I stared at the horse. The horse stared back with a corner of the letter hanging out its mouth. Fine. Gerald goes first then. Except Gerald refused because he'd never agreed to be a hero, he'd agreed to carry luggage, and now we were having a labour dispute outside a talking hole while somewhere in town the actual chosen one was getting a filling.
A wizard's day off
A wizard tries to rest.

He took his beard off and hung it on the hook by the door. I like that bit. Not sure what else he takes off. Hat obviously. Maybe all his magic lives in the beard so now it's doing spells at the coats and he has to get up again.
Reward offered
An adventure is badly advertised.

KILL GIANT RAT, said the notice. Rat wasn't giant. Town was tiny. I had already stepped on the blacksmith by the time anyone explained. Now I owed them a blacksmith and apparently couldn't leave until I'd learned the job.
Sword with opinions
A magical object is difficult to live with.

The sword kept telling me to avenge my father. My father was alive and ran a bakery. I explained this every morning. Every morning the sword said THE BLOOD MUST BE ANSWERED and I said yes well he's opened early today so you'll have to wait. I took it to the bakery in the end. Dad held it up to the light, said the edge was rubbish and used it to cut a loaf. The sword screamed. Not because of the bread, because apparently cutting anything counted as a sacred oath and now we were sworn to the loaf. Dad asked how long for. The sword didn't know. It had never happened before. I wanted to go home but the loaf had begun rising again even though it was cooked. There was a crack opening across the crust. Dad put a bowl over it and said we'll deal with that after lunch.
Hoard inventory
A dragon has a practical problem.

Sleeping on gold hurt his hips. Silver worse. Copper rash. Now the dragon slept beside the hoard pretending not to. Knight came in, started sorting coins by year. Dragon watched. Finally someone organising them. Waited an hour then coughed. Knight screamed and dropped everything together again. Dragon wanted to explain but the knight had started stabbing at his foot. Annoying rather than painful. He sat on him to make him stop. Hadn't thought past that.
Short cut spell
Magic solves the wrong problem.

I asked for the shortest way home. It made me shorter. Fine, badly phrased, my fault. Asked for the fastest route. Now I'm a very fast short person. The wizard said I had one wish left which was new infomation because he hadn't mentioned wishes at all, we'd been discussing spells and I had paid for a spell. I asked for my money back. Coins burst out my ears. Painful but at least I was rich for a minute until the wizard said service charge and swept half of them off the floor. I kicked his shin. Being short made the angle better. He kicked back and missed and I ran under the counter. There was a whole row of tiny shoes under there. So this was not the first time. I started shouting for the other customers to get out but the words came out as little paper birds and now I had that problem too.
Home after the quest
Return after an adventure.

They brought the head home in a sack. New king, old reward no longer valid. Head starting to smell. Teren said another king might buy it. Moth said all kings knew each other. They sat by the horse trough. Sack moved. Teren hit it. Moth said don't, if it's alive it might tell us where the treasure is. They should have thought of that days ago.
reserved apparently
Someone is sitting in your seat.

someone was in 14A and i had 14A on my tikcet so i did the awkward thing where you stand there holding it at chest height like a tiny warrant. he looked up and said this is 14A. yes i know. that is the issue. he showed his ticket, also 14A. same train same date. i was trying to be normal about it but he'd already taken his shoes off and i resented that more than the actual seat. the guard came and looked at both tickets and said one of you booked backwards. what does that even mean. then the train started moving the wrong way, not backwards along the track, sideways, through the people standing on the platform who didnt seem to notice. the man put his shoes back on very quickly and said let her have it.
missed it
A phone rings at an awkward time.

phone rang in the interview. i had put it on silent, i had, but the alarm app does its own thing and it was mum using the find my phone noise because i hadn't answered. i said sorry about five times while trying to turn it off. the woman interviewing me said is everything alright at home and i nearly said no just to make the noise seem worth it.
window face
See yourself unexpectedly.

saw my face in the dark train window and thought it was someone looking in. we're in a tunnel. obviously no one looking in. still moved seats. now i can see the old seat reflected behind me and its better if i dont look.
two coffees
Bring something for someone who doesn't arrive.

bought him the wrong coffee anyway. oat milk, might have been dan who liked that. kept it opposite so it looked like someone had gone to the toilet. woman next table asked me to watch her laptop. then his message came, cant today sorry. wanted to leave dramatically but i had custody of plumbing invoices. so just sat under the air vent with two cold coffees. shoudl have got my own milk right at least.
the green coat
Recognise someone by the wrong detail.

i followed the green coat off the bus. wasnt him. by the time i realised the doors had shut and my bag was still on the seat. ran after it for about ten seconds then stopped because what was the plan, catch a bus on foot. just stood there stupidly.
Conversation on the 38
A stranger starts a conversation.

she asked what i was reading and i said emails becasue i was reading emails. she said she loved that author. i didn't know what to do with that so i turned the phone slightly and said no sorry, email, from work. she nodded like i'd explained a complicated plot and asked if it was good. i said not especially. then she started telling me about a book she'd lost in 1987 and how she'd never found another copy. i was listening at first but my manager kept sending things and i was trying to reply without looking rude which made all the replies nonsense. i sent 'yes i can do thursday chapter' because she was saying chapter at the same time. manager sent a question mark. the woman had reached the part where the book turned out to be her husband's diary. i looked up properly then. she said she'd thrown it into the sea and had been looking in bookshops ever since, just in case. i wanted to ask why a diary would turn up in a bookshop but she was getting off and i had three more question marks from work.
terminates here
Stay on a train too long.

i woke up with my mouth open and a man tapping my shoulder. train ends here. here was not where i needed to be. i knew that from the trees, too many trees. i got off and the only other person on the platform was a kid with a cello case bigger than her. she asked me where we were. i pointed at the sign and she said no i mean why. like i might know why we'd both fallen asleep. the next train was in fifty minutes. she opened the case and there wasnt a cello just loads of oranges rolling about. i said oh. she said dont ask. i didnt, which is why i still don't have an ending for this.
Rust colour
Restore something old.

The rust came off in orange powder and underneath was more rust. Mara had expected bright metal, a reward for the work, but the chair seemed to be rust all the way through. She scrubbed harder. Her wrist ached. There was an insect living in the hollow leg and every time she tilted it the insect came out to look, then went back in. It had a white body and no obvious head. She tried not to think about it. The afternoon was thick, sticky, I mean the air was thick not the afternoon. She had promised the chair to someone and couldn't remember who. It was an excuse she'd given herself for bringing it home. A project. Something to do with her hands. Now her hands were orange and there was a hole where the seat joined the frame.
Tied too tight
A plant needs support.

She tied the rose to the wire and the wire to the post. By morning the rose had pulled the post out of the ground. Only an inch, but the square of fresh earth showed. She pushed it back with her heel. The thorns caught her sleeve. It had never flowered, this rose, just grown longer and longer canes that reached over the path like someone trying to find a light switch in the dark. That comparison doesn't work in daylight. She cut the longest cane and sap ran down her wrist. It was warm. She put the cut end in a jar for no reason she could explain. The leaves turned towards her as she carried it into the kitchen. Perhaps towards the window. She set the jar down and went outside for the shears, which she had left exactly where she'd been standing but could no longer see.
Colour sample
Choose a colour from a faded sample.

The blue on the card had faded green round the edges. I wanted that colour, the faded part. The man mixed proper blue. I said no, older. He added grey. It wasn't the same but I didn't know how to keep explaining.
Glasshouse in rain
An abandoned place is still being used.

The glasshouse had no glass above the door and too much glass on the ground. Ferns grew through the shelves. On one shelf someone had made a bed from old sacks, with a folded jumper at the top where a pillow would be. Mara stayed at the entrance. Rain ticked on the panes that remained, uneven because some were plastic and some were real glass. She had come to take photographs for the estate agent. In the lens the bed looked like a pile of rubbish and she understood how easy it would be to make it disappear without moving anything, just by choosing the other angle. She lowered the camera. There were shoes under the shelf, wet at the toes. A carrier bag hung from a nail, twisting slightly although she couldn't feel any wind. She called hello. It sounded too loud and too cheerful. No one answered. She called again, this time like a question, and from somewhere behind the ferns came the sound of somebody carefully setting a cup down. She looked at the photograph she'd already taken. In the small screen everything was green and the bed was almost invisible.
Drawer
Something broken becomes familiar.

The handle was gone so she pulled the drawer open by putting two fingers in the holes. There should be something in the drawer. A letter maybe. No, that's always what is in a drawer in stories. Batteries. Just batteries and an old takeaway menu. I can't get past that.
Watering nothing
Keep a routine after it loses its purpose.

She kept watering the empty pot. The plant had died in June. In August the soil dipped in the middle. She added more. Dipped again. Water disappeared with a sucking sound. Tipped it out onto newspaper. A narrow hole went through the solid soil, right down to the tiles. I want that hole to go somewhere. But maybe it's just where the root was.
Rectangle
A house remembers where something stood.

Behind the cupboard the wall was yellow. Everything else had gone white over the years. A rectangle of the room as it used to be, though she couldn't remember choosing yellow. It was such an ugly yellow. Almost mustard but sickly.
Cutting before leaving
Save a piece of something you cannot keep.

She took cuttings from the hedge because the new owners were going to pull it out. Six cuttings wrapped in wet kitchen roll, then a seventh because one of the first six was bent. The hedge had scratched her face every summer for twenty years. She hated it. That didn't seem to matter now. The man with the van asked if she wanted the cracked pot as well. She said no, then yes, then no because she had no garden at the new place. He put it in anyway. She stood on the path with the cuttings getting warm in her hand and looked at the bare patch where the pot had been. Slugs had made a whole town under it. They were moving slowly into the light, no idea what had happened, and she found herself putting a bit of cardboard down for them.
Minutes of the flat meeting
Housemates attempt to make rules.

We agreed the person who finishes the milk buys the next milk. Then we had to define finishes because Ben had left enough to wet a spoon and claimed that wasn't finished. Thirty minutes on this. I had come prepared to discuss the mould. Nobody wanted to discuss the mould because the mould was in my room and therefore apparently my personal hobby. Lisa suggested a rota. We already had a rota. It was on the fridge behind three other rotas from previous attempts at having a rota. Ben said he couldn't do Tuesdays. No one had mentioned Tuesdays. I wrote MILK in capitals on the paper and underlined it until the pen went through. We ordered takeaway halfway through and used the milk money to pay for it. I realise that sounds like a punchline but it actually just made another problem we still had to discuss.
Camera on
Try to look professional in an unsuitable place.

The only place with decent wifi was the bathroom so I put the laptop on a laundry basket and angled it above the toilet. Fine. Professional. Plain white background. Then someone upstairs flushed and the pipes made the noise of a dying ship directly behind my head. I said sorry there's building work. There wasn't building work. My boss said her husband was a plumber and asked what sort. I said structural, which is not plumbing but she nodded. Then the cat climbed into the basket and the laptop tilted slowly forwards while I was explaining quarterly targets. I caught it with both hands. Camera showed the ceiling, then my chin, then the toilet with the lid up because I hadn't thought that far ahead. Nobody said anything. That was worse than somebody saying something. I finished the targets looking at five very still faces and one person who had turned their camera off, presumably to laugh with freedom.
Easy care
Buy something you cannot look after.

Bought a cactus because they thrive on neglect. It died. Apparently there are different types of neglect and mine was too advanced. Pot's useful though. Put pens in it. Still get stabbed by the dead cactus because I haven't actually removed it.
Taking the bin out
A simple task expands.

Bin bag split at the door. Coffee, eggshell, receipt for a blender. We don't have a blender. Ben can't afford internet apparently but can afford a blender. Found it hidden behind rice. Planned a whole confrontation, then neighbour needed to get past the rubbish. Cleaned that up first. Lost the speech. Put the receipt by his keys instead, which is how all our arguments happen now. Little bits of evidence waiting for somebody to pretend not to see them.
Password hint
A system rejects something you know.

The hint was 'you know this'. Very helpful, past me. I did not know this. Tried the dog, the old dog, the street, the street spelled wrong because I'd lived there two years before learning it had two Ls. Locked out. I wrote a new hint on paper: don't be clever. Put the paper somewhere safe. Immediately couldn't remember where.
A quiet night in
A relaxing evening becomes complicated.

I had plans to do nothing and people don't respect that as a plan. Ben asked if I could help move a wardrobe. I said I was busy. He asked doing what. Nothing. He looked at me. I looked at him. The wardrobe was in the hallway already so this was less a request than an announcement of the next hour of my life. We got it round one corner and it stopped. Not stuck exactly, the walls were touching it on both sides but it could still move backwards, except there was a second wardrobe behind us because he'd bought two. I asked why two. He said they were a set. Of wardrobes. A set. I sat down on the floor in the small triangle of space left beside the first one and opened the film on my phone. He said I wasn't helping. I said that had been my original position and I was pleased we had finally reached an understanding. Then someone rang the doorbell and neither of us could get to it. We ignored it for a while but they kept ringing and I remembered I'd ordered food before all this started.
